This will be a very personal review tied to my personal experience.Concord deserved so much better. My honest opinion, it was fun, I loved getting to play hero shooter which was not following the f2p formula and it was a fresh breath of air after all the years Ive spent in Overwatch. To call it a clone is to admit you didnt understand the core mechanics of the game.There were little to no team synergy as which characters built the best team or even a team doomed to lose and instead it focused on player synergy. You played your characters in the order you wanted to obtain buffs provided by their class, creating your optimal build for your favorite freegunner. It was team-based but you are the one looking out for yourself making sure you achieve your ultimate build while securing kills or the objective. There was no classic healers for you to blame if you died. Where there were classes suited for a tank role or support roles, everyone is more or less a DPS with who can fend for themselves but the game did reward those who played in a coordinated unit. The game had a slower TTK removing everyone's ability to one-shot to allow you to play out your cooldowns rather than the first person to spot the other player wins. This was up my alley but its not for those who enjoy a more sim-like experience. No character felt obnoxiously balanced at launch while Teo was quite insane during Beta but keep in mind these types of games cannot be 100% balanced but I think this game was pretty well rounded. While there were a couple of characters which were on the stronger side, during the time it didnt feel as obnoxious as Overwatch could feel at times although I can see how time would offer times in the game where balance could prove a challenge as balancing these sort of games is nothing to scuff at.I loved my time on Bazz which was my favourite character. Shes not a character im drawn to in games per usual as Im typically a support main but I loved her hyper aggressive nature and I built her to favour range and speed, sometimes with improved dodge and reload on top if I couldnt access my build by my favoured freegunners. It was a blast!I enjoyed the selection of maps to play on. During beta it didnt feel enough but once launch game around there were enough maps for me to not make it feel repetitive during the time I played. Train troubles were my favourite of the maps as it offered a fun level of tunnels and elevated angles. All maps were mirror based like arenas and if it eventually would have had more game modes I wouldve liked to see maps that were less arena likes.The game modes were pretty standard with the exception of the single spawn game mode, that one was unique to Concord and the most competitive mode and ideal if you had a communicating 5 stack. I spent most of my time in the objective based modes which were not as hard core as single spawn but had more to offer than just TDM which were my least preferred mode.The character designs were unique and their fashion could be really out there which was cool to see in a sci-fi as it makes me feel like this is not set in my time and their fashion has different values than the ones from my time such as how historically men wore high heels while today that has flipped. The more simpler designs opened up for more skin possibilities down the line and silhouettes were all distinct and and characters had unique movement animations even down to their dodge. I would have liked to see less humanoid aliens down the line as we have seen non humanoid characters function in shooters in the past such as Overwatch so there is where I would like to see more creative liberties taken. At launch I didnt think the skins were the strongest but there were still skins that stuck out as great, the legendary It-Z skin for example looked great while Jabali's legendary suffered the same issue as Overwatch's Junkerqueen's legendary skins did at launch where they are different but they do the same thing as the default skin, like it is two different concept arts for the same skin.For pronouns which was apparently a point of contention, idk why people are fighting over it when at the same time use pronouns for Star Wars robots and droids or even boats which has been done for generations.In conclusion for me, Concord was another hero shooter, it had a few elements unique to its structure, it wasnt industry changing but nor did I expect it to be just as I do not expect any upcoming MMO to the a WoW killer or hard rival, just something more for us gamers to play and enjoy to provide variety to the market and Concord did that for me. Concord was its own take on the genre and I am very disappointed It didnt get the marketing it deserved. Like any game Concord wasnt for everyone, I have yet to find a game that is, its just a shame how we have to build factions of hate and ridicule around games and cheer when people lose their jobs and communities the game they enjoyed together. Not everyone who disliked Concord took part in this but I saw it in many places on the internet and it breaks my heart. I feel for anyone having to go through this with any game. Concord is not the first and wont be the last.I wish the developers and the Concord community the best. I enjoyed my time with you and I never wanted the forced Steam refund to come through. To me you deserved to keep the money even with my limited playtime. I clearly saw your hard work and dedication and on top of that a really awesome community rare to competitive multiplayer games. You guys rock, thank you for a great few weeks its been a pleasure and I'm so sad to see it end.

Well. It's dead, and there is still money in my pocket. Oh Concord :/ It's a 6/10 at worst, and I'm genuinely gonna miss the hero mechanics in this game. Did this need to take 8 years to develop? And while I can't totally disagree with that sentiment, there was a solid game here, if nothing that would set the world on fire.Sony and the rest need to stop spending hundreds of millions on the "Games as a service" model for every single genre of game. Game budgets are getting out of control and failure is just getting more and more expensive. We don't want you to play it safe, we want you to scale back these gargantuan rehashes of the same formulas to a level where you can actually maintain them if the player-base doesn't hit 50k concurrent players in the first week of it's life. All of the marketing and CGI promos won't save a game if the audience can get a similar experience elsewhere for cheaper. If this had shipped with any sort of substantial offline content, Sony probably wouldn't be in this mess right now.All that being said, I wish Firewalk studios luck with whatever happens next. Regardless of how mismanaged this project was, there is genuine talent there, and it shows despite it's flaws.

Edit: Mass refunds and a shut down in under a month. WowTLDR: Game is a ton of fun but I can't recommend someone spend $40 on it at this moment. If the game is made free to play, or goes on a decent sale, I would recommend.Elephant in the room, player count. People will cope and say queues are still fast but that is only because there is 0 SBMM and no region locking WITH crossplay default enabled. Even still the no respawn mode (Rivalry) has long queues at all times, sometimes nobody queuing it at all. Speaking of Rivalry, players throwing to quickly farm XP has been an issue since launch weekend and devs have done nothing to fix it, they've been silent post launch. This makes the mode only playable with a full stack, which will lead to you 4-0'ing every match, at least in my experience. Suffice it to say the playercount is a massive issue. While the numbers are for sure better on playstation, I have serious doubts that they would even be called good, I suspect there is sub 500 players online at any given time as of 2 weeks post launch.This leaves the other 2 respawn queues, TDM/Kill Confirmed and Domination/Hardpoint. These are both fun and I enjoy both, but there are issues with these modes. TDM matches are always far too short, the kill count should be increased from 30 to 50. Kill Confirmed is actually great, I don't have a suggested change for it. Domination and Hardpoint are both balanced around constant contesting. 2 good teams will lead to long matches where both teams struggle to garner a significant lead. A missmatched lobby will lead to quick games with score gaps of 100+. When these games go the distance they are great fun. Unfortunately due to the lack of SBMM, no doubt further impacted by the low player count, these long high quality matches are not the norm.The core gameplay here is fantastic. Destiny PVP but way better. People compare this to Overwatch a lot but it plays nothing like that. Healing for example is very slow, so fights can end very quickly despite the generally long TTK if you don't play with your team or stand in the open. There are so many small details here that are very clever and do a lot to make basic hero shooter mechanics more engaging. A quick example is how this game does ability recharging. Every ability is unique in this regard. Some are on a timer like normal, others require kills, others pickups, and others character specific things like getting a scan with a different ability and interacting with that again. There are tons of small twists like this on the standard multiplayer hero shooter formula and almost all of them are great changes. The best way to engage with these systems is in the Rivalry mode, especially the crew bonus system that rewards swapping characters, but unfortunately Rivalry is kind of ruined by previously mentioned issues.People really don't like the character designs. I'm probably 50/50 like/hate on the roster. I really like some of the character designs like Kyps and Jabali, but then there are huge stinkers like Daw and Bazz (although when you unlock different glasses for Bazz she is way better IMO). There is 0 sex appeal here, which I think is what has most people upset even though they would never admit it. Whether or not this matters a ton is is up to you. For me this is not a major issue, I play these kind of games for the gameplay and if it looked like Roblox with fancy lighting and effects I wouldn't really care. Aside from character models the game looks very good IMO.Tech wise I've only had some infrequent crashing and small bugs. I am on a 4070ti Super with an AMD 7800x3D though so I can't really comment on performance. Runs good for me, might not on a worse setup.Im a Sci Fi guy, big on Star Wars pre Disney and I love Mass Effect. This games lore/world has a lot to like. You can read about an astonishing amount of things in the "Galactic Guide", essentially this games prettier version of the mass effect codex. Unfortunately there is no voice acting here so it is a lot of reading. Some sneak peeks here: The entire galaxy is slowly being consumed by something called the tempest, the pseudo galaxy government known as the guild is consuming the finite resources without having a plan for when they run out, and most of the food people eat are giant squid like creatures from another planet doused in grounded up egg goo that makes it taste good. People dismiss this mode, but I think its a great addition and its clear that a lot of effort has been put into this. Were this game to have a long lifespan (which I seriously doubt at this point) there would be so many cool ways for the story to go. You can also read this while you are in queue which is very nice.There are also the weekly "vignettes" but both featured so far were also in the beta so this has been extremely underwhelming as of now.With the $40 price tag some promises were made and there was also some automatic expectations. I have been overall disappointed with the value for my money when it comes to this. One thing that was promised thanks to the price tag was no paid battle pass, which is true come launch. Progression in this game is based on your account level and individual character level. Both account and character levels earn you separate rewards. Unfortunately a lot of the rewards you will be earning here are underwhelming. Trinkets seen as battle pass filler in other games still make their appearance here despite the lack of battlepass. Here they serve as progression filler so they can tell you there is a reward in the next few levels when all it ends up being is a weapon charm you probably won't even bother to equip. There are also a TON of re-colours.Furthermore a lot of the "big" rewards you will eventually earn like legendary skins kind of suck. Like the character designs, legendary skins are probably 50/50 good/bad. Emari's is great and fixes a character who I don't like the regular look of. Meanwhile Jabali's biggest change is some horns on his hat. Despite some of these underwhelming rewards levelling also takes a SIGNIFICANT amount of time. With 60 hours in the game as of writing (5 or so being afk or accidentally left on) I still do not have a single character at level 20, and multiple still not at level 10. My account level is only just 50, with the hardest achievement in the game being to reach account level 100. I have only seen one of these legendary skins in the wild during a match. Progression could be 2x as fast and I would still probably think its a bit slow, but that would be a great improvement.There is a cosmetic shop coming with the season 1 patch scheduled for October (although we will see how this schedule holds given the games launch), and I will be very upset if a bunch of way cooler skins are added with it and nothing else is added to the games current progression.I don't regret buying the game, I expected to only get 2 months or so out of it as casual shooter game I could play on the side, but I didn't think the numbers would be THIS bad. As a Destiny 2 Crucible player, there are many things I like about Concord, yet I cannot in good consciousness leave a positive review due to some fundamental issues with the launch version of the game.First, the obvious problem is a lack of players. This means when you do find a game, you will most likely find the same players. There can be no doubt that Concord has really clicked for a dozen of players, which you will find out, when your entire team of level 2 accounts blindly rushes into the open, to get absolutely destroyed in seconds. I suppose the only upside of the long queue times, is that by the time people actually get into a game, the Steam refund window will be closed.Many reviewers have already commented on the bland character designs, which is very disappointing considering the rich worldbuilding, gorgeous environments and Bungie skyboxes. I am willing to bet my Canadian pesos that if you show a random person a picture of Teo, they would be hard pressed to tell you which game he's from. The character design is not just a failure in an aesthetic sense: given that many of the crucial roles are so visually unappealing, in random games (the only ones you can currently play due to the aforementioned lack of players) everyone will lock down the same 4 or 5 characters, which results in poor team compositions. Now I am not saying that every game needs anime waifus, but it is very important to make support and tank characters visually appealing, so that people would want to pick them. Meanwhile, players will be wondering how the hell Daw passed military qualification, lock down Star Child, and then rush into a chokepoint to get instantly obliterated.For a $40 game, the customisation is simply not there. Each character will have 5-6 recolours, and a low-effort legendary skin that will often be somehow worse than the default outfit. For a game with such high production values, it is puzzling that the developers have spent no effort on making cosmetics unlocks visually-appealing. By comparison, if you were to spend that money on a couple of season passes for the Free-to-Play games Concord is attempting to compete with, you will end up with a bunch of outrageous, distinct outfits that probably play the sad whale song each time you score a kill.In Concord, you can unlock variants of the 16 classes through five sets of objectives, with some variants being significantly stronger than the starting loadouts. I am definitely not a fan of this system, and it feels like a cheap way to add unlockables instead of designing a comprehensive loadout system: some guns just don't feel great, and it would be great to have some gear customisation options, instead of avoiding a character because their one weapon sucks. Yes, I get the game balance angle, but surely Concord have enough combined experience making PVP games to balance about 18 different guns!The gunplay is mostly satisfying, some maps are quite good, and there is a lot of good game design, which makes Concord encounters interesting and enjoyable. Nonetheless, with all these issues, I just can't recommend the game and, by the time you read this review, the game will simply not have enough players to be worth saving. Also, and this can't be stressed enough, this game took 8 years to make. WHY??

While the rough core of the game isnt bad and there is a semblence of a stable foundation, the game doesnt innovate and even is missing critical systems needed for a multiplayer game. In this rough shape and at this price, the game has a serious problem to get the attention of potentional players as its presentation is at best lukewarm and the gameplay lacks all common improvements present in the gaming scene in the past years. Due to various issues listed bellow, I cannot recommend this game at this current state and price. I personally will keep playing the game, but with these issues, I cannot recommend it.[b]Gameplay[/b]The core of the gameplay is present and if this is your first game of this type, it may feel fresh at first, but it is lacking larger and smaller QoL improvements. One of them is partial weapon reloads, there are too many instances where you can accidentaly interrupt the realoding animation and once you want to resume it, it begin from the start. A smaller QoL feature that is missing is Assist counting as kills, this is needed in high latency lobbies. The game gas a weird long time to kill, which I am personaly not fan of.[b]In-game communication[/b]The game has a basic pinging system and an option to opt-in into voice chat at the start of the match and that is it. The game lacks a communication wheel to say simple commands to your team like "Group up", "I need healing" or even "Thank you". Chat is not present at all. This team oriented game has almost no ways how to communicate as a team.[b]Crew system[/b]I feel this system is at the core the cause of the character balance issues. Some characters are strong from the get go and these feel good to play. But other you first need to apply bonuses by playing different characters and by that time in the match, you have no assurance that the actual character you want to play isnt already taken (and there is no way to tell other players you want to switc to said character). Basicaly if you wan to play a strong character, you do not need to use the crew system. If you want to play a weaker character, you first need to switch trough various different characters to make the one you want to play less bad and you will still play worse than the good characters.[b]Game modes[/b]The game has 3 playlists, Brawl, Overrun and Rivarly.Brawl consist of TDM and TDM+ (kill confirmed)Overrun consist of Capture the zones, and capture the moving zoneRivalry is a no respawn gamemode, but I never got to play it.Brawl and Overrun plays the same and most people ignore the objectives in Overrun as there is no incentive from the game to play objectives. There is no Capture the Flag, no Paylod, no Push, no PvE, no Deathmatch.[b] Multiplayer and queue times[/b]About a week has passed since the release of the game and depending on the time of day, you may get a quick queue time in about 30 seconds, but if you are on PC and in the EU, you may experience queue times of 2 - 3 minutes even for the most played "Brawl" playlist. And if you get into a match, be prepared to be places into a high latency lobby. I wasnt able to get into "Rivalry" playlist as the queue times went above 6 minutes and I gave up.[b]Progression and unlocks[/b]Most progression objectives are a variation of number of kills, assist, damage done, rounds played, rounds won. The progression system has minimal teamwork oriented objectives and so far none related to capturing a zone or any tied more to the gamemodes.The game doesnt show you what item you unlock at what level, it only shows what is the current item to be unlocked, but you have no idea if the next one is something """interesting""" or another side bar color.[b] Characters (gameplay wise)[/b]16 characters and a lot of them feels unbalanced. You get strong characters that can stand on their own like Lennox and Haymar, and on the other end of the spectrum you get Jabali with his BB gun. The overall issue is that some characters have a really low damage output and if you are in a high latency lobby and experiencing high ping and lost packets, playing those characters is misery.[b]Characters (lore wise)[/b]The game is unable to sell the personas of the characters to the players. There is no banter between characters at the start of the match that would tell you what the relation between each character is. So if you are not drawn in by the looks of the characters, there isnt much else to know about them. The only info you get is an entry which you get by leveling a character to level 3, but as of now, it only talks about their backstory.[b]Characters (visualy)[/b]Most of the characters designs feels like they need more iterations befoure they could be considered good. Some designs are just too much, like the design of Bazz would benefit from a streamlining.[b]Custom games[/b]There is no option to host your own lobby.[b]Lore[/b]One of the selling point of the game is its lore and how it is presented in the Galactic Guide. While the visual presentation is nice in a form of a galactic map, the game does a very poor job of connecting said lore to the gameplay. The lore set up the freegunners as oponnents to the Guild, but there is no hint of that in the gameplay at all as all is freegunners fighting each other.The game has [b]vignetters (CGI shorts)[/b] which plays at the start of the game, but only the newest one plays and otherwise they are not present in the game at all and you need to do your own homework to find them.There are also [b]Freegunners adventtures shorts (animated shorts)[/b] which are not in the game, there is no mention of them in the game and you need to be lucky to find them.

A seemingly rushed development that resulted in a bland, quickly processed product that is more quantity than quality. It's extremely unoptimized (averaging 30-40 fps on a 7900 XTX w/ 64GB of RAM, & on NVME).Even if you can get past the performance issues, the game has MAJOR balancing issues between its heroes. For example, Flark's gun is a complete abomination of a weapon that shoots floaty projectiles that do almost nothing for damage, whereas some other characters are running around one-tapping with their weapons. The time-to-kill ratio is VERY fast. For it to be this fast in a hero shooter, there *has* to be some modicum of health regen! Health pickups throughout maps are few and far between. Class-based systems are not emphasized ('Oh, big guy? Must be a tank. Oh, little guy with assault rifle? Must be a DPS...Wait, healer? healer?') You're kind of just left guessing about what to even do or how to strategize (Ironically, the game's training mode is quite enjoyable).It's 2 core game modes to boot are a standard TDM and Area Control, which is basically Domination? Not bad game modes per se, just not something you would expect from this kind of game. This is something you see in a game like Rogue Company from Hi-Rez, which is completely free to play (and this is a $40-$60 title).It's a shame because this game's design is fairly charming, almost feels like a Guardians of the Galaxy meets Overwatch type of hero shooter, but....it's riddled with technical issues that keep it from reaching its full potential.Maybe they'll turn it around? idk, but where it currently sits from a developmental standpoint, it seems like its A LOT to ask for. Great game. Solid gunplay and movement, easily on par with its competitors if not exceeding. At the time of writing, Concord has around 250 concurrent players on a weekday and 400 on a solid weekend. There's a lot of speculation and brain-gazing being done to explain why this AAA major release hero shooter, which had over one hundred million dollars placed into production/development, flopped. Gamergate wannabes and Grumz' lil crew of pronoun-hating slop warriors couldn't possibly have enough leverage to deal a multi-million dollar blow to Sony corporation, surely, right? Instead, the issue has to lay elsewhere, much like the Death Star, there is a critical flaw in Concord's production that led to this historical triple-A flop-piece.So where is this flaw? It isn't the gameplay, which is sharp, responsive, and contains depth in multitudes of characters with all variety of mechanical kits. We have tanks, damage carries, utility abusers, movement fiends, healers, and more! The game modes are solid and the balance isn't particularly terrible, although if you play for long you start to notice damage-dealing squishies are a lil overtuned. You'll likely notice this while playing their most popular playlist, Overrun, an unlimited respawn and objective-based playlist, which plays similarly to quick play in rival games. It is my personal belief that this is core to the issue Concord is experiencing, specifically, I believe the game was built, balanced, and designed around their competitive limited-respawn game mode called Rivalry and that it shows blatantly through the complete disregard for the typical hero shooter meta/team comps in Overrun.Due to balances being done around Rivalry and thus limited respawn as the primary game mode, I believe a lot of the weight, consistency, and effort put into team comps, metas, and other organized interactions with the game are disregarded entirely by players. Since there is no rank to achieve and there is no punishment for playing off-cuff flashy and dangerous, you won't find any players learning or even caring about a genuine effort toward competitive play. Most lobbies have instant locks on all major damage-dealing squishes because ultimately, due to unlimited respawns, short respawn timers, and lack of incentive, all players play Concord more as an individual-led arena shooter than a team-based hero shooter.This, combined with Sony's complete disregard for marketing their product, is the cause of Concord's flop. It effectively has no spine and lacks a path forward to forcing players into taking the game, its meta, and its unique competitive features seriously. Concord has/will continue to be thoroughly punished for attempting something unique in a genre that is intentionally stale due to the fickle nature of competitive gamers. There is absolutely no way for Sony to force us to play the game properly and it pains me greatly to state I do not believe the player base will care enough to examine their gameplay habits and realize they are ignoring the most impressive, unique, and thoughtful features the game has to offer as a result.Sony screwed up majorly by not properly advertising/marketing this game, but it is the stubborn and often thoughtless nature of media consumption that robs us of a unique take on such a stagnating genre.Overall / TLDR - The game is good. Very good. $40 is a bit much to ask for, but there is a lot of effort put into the game mechanically, narratively, and creatively. It is pretty to look at, fun to play, and has tons of lore for a dork to dig into, which is admirable, given the complete disregard for story/characters rivals in the genre have. The issue is more so a disconnect between the developer's intentions towards the game and the player base blatantly not caring, preventing outstandingly unique mechanics in the game from being appreciated/used properly.

As a lover of hero-shooters, I decided to give Concord a chance despite the horrendous feedback it's gotten. I'm at the age where I know far better than to listen to the masses when it comes to these sort of things. So give it a shot I did, and what came next shocked me.You see I grew up on console games. Goin back all the way to the Atari, as my folks both loved gaming themselves. I've been entrenched in the love for digital realms since the age of 3 and onward. Although many things have changed, many so too stayed the same. The feeling of wonder being one of them. Although rare, sometimes, if you're lucky you're afforded that sense of being that carries your mind to places you'd forgotten ever were. That brought you a sense of peace and excitement, only renewed. Now I know what you're thinking "cmon, Dream, you're hyping this up way too much", and sure perhaps to some it may sound that way; though if I may... To those of you who grew up on mp console shooters. The Perfect Darks, Jetforce Geminis, and Goldeneye (to name a few), the feeling of having a tight knit multiplayer experience, that's what Concord offers. Opinionated, but rarely do I find pleasure from games anymore. It's all been done, done and done again many times over. Nothing is original anymore, nothing has the ability to be, but to capture what made the classics great still has value.Beyond the shooting, which is solid. Beyond the abilities, which are fun and even beyond the environments, which are unique and make the mind wander in thought... Concord has a feel to it. A sense of wonder hidden just underneath this quaint package of mp fun. There's a story here, a living, breathing universe. The developers, despite the hate are not hacks by any means. They've weaved something beautiful. Something deserving of life, and to be explored to who knows what heights. A part of me wishes they expressed it with more depth. Perhaps story missions. Travelling the stars, exploring planets. This game has the framework for that adventure, and that's what I mean by the sense of wonder. There is so much more to be told. The Galactic Guide tells a story of a Galaxy Wide framework of supposed good vs evil, and the intricacies that are in play between them. The free man vs the enslaved. The rich and the poor. It offers a glimpse into the daily lives, what keeps things running the way they do and what it all means to be a Free Gunner. Needless to say I am a space nerd and absolutely love this aspect of the game. It not only is incredibly relevant to our lives, but It centers the experience, grounding it with substance. Though, as it stands, all of this is bottled within the confines of PVP matches. Be it TDM, OBJ or Competitive. A shame, really, but it's done relatively well and I truly have high hopes for what's to come. If Sony holds on and allows Concord to mature, I can't help but be excited for the future. Exploring the storylines of the characters, a path moving forward to face off against the guild, if even possible. New characters, maps and perhaps even modes. All of it could come together so well, If only given the chance. We'd have an experience filled with nostalgia and wonder, and take it from me, that's not so easy to come by. So here's to hoping.But yeah, there's my view on Concord as it stands, for what it's worth, and I meant every word. I didn't receive the game for free, and I'm not invested in either side of the political nonsense that has ruined just about every facet of life. Nor am I sponsored or in contact with the developers in any way imaginable. This is just me, a gamer, and my opinion of the experience afforded. Take it as you will. Here's to all you risk takers that turned a blind eye to the hate. Thanks for allowing this seasoned gamer to feel that sense of wonder again, and to all that may come.Oh, right, and lastly... The music in the Galactic Guide is enchanting beyond words. Definitely should give it a listen sometime if you haven't already. Total 80s space vibe like you wouldn't believe.

Concord never had it easy, and with the rumors of toxic ideals and workplace environment at Firewalk Studios, it's not a surprise the game ended up how it did. It's fun, and I enjoy it playing it; despite of the woke/pronouns noise sorrounding it, despite of the bad performance on my otherwise decent machine; and despite some of its questionable design choices.The "crew bonus"-system is interesting, as your played characters will give you a permanent bonus when you die and switch off of it. It promotes more varied gameplay experiences within the match, and provides a helping hand to the losing team, as they will be able to go through more characters and rack up more bonuses. It's interesting in concept, but at the same time, Concord wants to have short matches that last about 4 to 5 mintues, so unless you get off to a really bad start and die a few times within the first few minutes, you rarely get to really leverage the power you've built up, as the matches are usualy over before you get to take advantage of said bonuses. I wish they increase the average match duration by 3 to 4 minutes, because aside from my gripes with the system itself, sometimes the downtime between matches is equal to the duration of the actual matches themselves.While I have a little handful of characters I have yet to try out, luckily I can say that the ones I have tried (which are the majority of the cast) are fun to play. They're pretty simple to pick up and play, while some have slight variances in mechanics from others that confuse at first, like some recharge their abilities based on cooldowns, others have to get takedowns and then pickup a charge from the enemy's corpse, and others have to go through a lengthy recharge animation to get another charge of their abilities.I hope Concord can turn things around and find a healthy audience, because looking at the game itself in a vacuum, it deserves it, but I'm not so confident it will, because of the internal challenges Firewalk Studios have to overcome to be able to right the ship.

Look you're going to hear a lot of negative buzz coming from culture warriors on the internet. I don't care about culture wars, I care about how good a game is. And this game is REALLY good.This game, unlike what keeps being parroted, is a mix of Destiny/Halo and Team Fortress 2, not OW or Marvel Rivals. This means you should expect a much more shooting based experience than a hero based experience. There are no ults so all the fights feel fair and your good aim will be rewarded with practically every character. The classes are not designed the traditional way, so there isn't a mandatory healer or tank as every class can deal damage and there are health packs around the map. In short, this is very much inspired on older shooters and not hero shooters or twitchier options with very fast paced action that are hitting the market by the dozen nowadays.On the polish front, it's what you expect from Sony (and I hate most of their games, before anyone assumes I'm glazing). The graphics are some of the best in the market for a shooter, if not THE best, the sound is insanely well made both from a readability and a quality perspective (and the OST is pretty cool too), the UI elements are clean and in that 80s futuristic theme the game clearly draws from, the shooting and movement feel impactful and deliberate like in older Halo games. On this front, I think most people would be hard pressed to disagree so there isn't much point elaborating much. Watch a video of the game and it's pretty clear it's up to Sony's standards on the polish side of things.Now outside of that, it's also important for you to know that at the present I've had 0 trouble finding matches in seconds during the day and up to 5ish minutes late at night on the more "competitive" mode which has fewer players due to that nature. That's because unlike what people keep repeating with the Steam numbers, 8/9 out of 10 players in every lobby (myself included) are on PS5. That means that the visibility Steam numbers give is pretty low, because the vast vast VAST majority of people isn't accounted for.Not all is perfect with the game of course. Some of the character designs are rather uninspired (moreso the attires than the characters themselves, in my opinion), there could be a bigger variety of game modes, games outside of Rivalry (the more competitive mode) are kinda short right now, the game lacks a bit in social aspects with no text chat and opt-in voice chat and the new player onboarding experience could still be a bit more thorough given all the systems the game includes to give a fresh take on the shooter genre (variants, class bonuses, crew building, hero selection limitations in Rivalry, etc). But even with those issues, this is one of the most fun shooters I've played in a LONG while, and if you're a fellow old, you'll appreciate a game that isn't catered to all the zoomers moving around at the speed of sound but instead harkens back to the days of Halo 3 and "weightier" arena shooters.I can also say that I've experienced no tech issues with everything maxed out (DLSS on quality mode) on a 4070 Super and a i7-12700K, which is definitely not top of the line. Not discrediting people who did experience issues, but a lot of reviews make it sound like everyone's having issues and that is not the case.I highly recommend the game and hope it keeps growing so that it gets the recognition it deserves. It would be a massive tragedy if a really good game doesn't make it because people decided to start a crusade against things that are in no way related to what matters most: the gameplay.

It's frustrating, but maybe I just need to invest some more time to get used to it.The game modes are fine, but the main issue the game has is its pricing. [b] TL/DR: [/b] Very fun, if not very innovative, PVP shooter with a strong foundation. Whether it is able to grow into something special remains to be seen.If you're a fan of Destiny PVP, but don't have the time/interest in grinding for the best weapons to stay competitive, then you'll love this. Lots of Destiny DNA in here, even plenty of fun lore entries for those that like to read supplemental story stuff. Lots of movement + abilities feel taken straight from the crucible.Mechanically, the game has a great foundation and while apparently not for everyone I'm a big fan of the art style. Has a similar vibe to the art direction Alien franchise in the "sci-fi but make it kinda shitty" that I love, but trade Alien's grim realism for bright colors and lightheartedness. Characters as a whole all feel pretty balanced and worthwhile using, without anyone necessarily feeling MUST HAVE in all scenarios.Something the game does that's notably different from others in its genre are stacking passive perks that you gain by switching character archetypes throughout a match, which encourages swapping up your heroes and strategically earning buffs that will most benefit the next character. Several characters also have an emphasis on deployables, which unlike most games of its ilk do not go away when you switch hero's or die. A complete valid strategy is to pick a character with the sole purpose of littering the field with their gadget before swapping to one you're more comfortable with for combat.Unfortunately, it really does seem like just a solid foundation currently. The game type variety is pretty lacking and none of the game modes feel like they fit thematically as a crew running jobs together. I'd love to see some game types that are maybe multi-objective or feel more "job" oriented (defend/attack heist style missions, escort/assassinate a VIP, etc).One other area that could be improved is in round banter between characters, or specifically the current lack thereof. One character will say a line at the beginning of a round, but that's about it. Mimicking Overwatch's storytelling through in round character dialogue/banter would be a smart play, especially if they're wanting to lean into narrative like it seems.Other QOL of things that would go a long in no particular order:[list][*]Better Ping system[*]Ability to Multi-queue for game modes[*]Longer rounds (they frequently feel like they're ending just as they heat up)[*] Better skins to chase, currently only one skin is interesting per character, with the rest just palette swaps.[/list]Despite a laundry list of things that could be improved and added I can't stress enough though that the game is FUN. In it's current state I'm still finding myself wanting to jump in one more match and learn how to use a new hero better. The game is good, but currently not great. The potential is there though, and ball is in the studios court to see how they handle updates and the live service elements of the game.

I have put in a refund request.I would like to state the fact that there were lots of talented hard working people who contributed to this game over almost a decade and a lot of their work is great, however a lot of it also deserves criticism.With that being said however, let's start with the gameplay of Concord.The base game is fun, as is basically any other arena shooter. The gun play is good, hit registration seemed fine and the levels felt well designed. The hero abilities are fine as well with some actually unique ones that do spice up the gameplay a bit. It does rely a bit on teamwork and while that does make sense, expecting randoms to cooperate with you is like expecting Sony to make good financial decisions. There are a few modes, but don't expect to play all of them because of the lack of players.While the basics are good and it's a pretty fun game, I don't see why anyone would pay 40$ when they can get this experience, likely more fully fledged, by playing something else. It's a fun but generic game. OK is the word that best describes it, maybe in a slight apathetic tone. It doesn't expand on anything, nothing here feels brand new, just generic fine hero shooter pvp with a Guardians of The Galaxy theme slapped on it (focus on the word "slapped" as it feels like a copy but more on that a bit later). Leaving a review because I think the game and its devs are receiving a disproportionate amount of hate.[list][*][b]Price[/b]: Single price tag and you can unlock all content including post-launch content. A lot of people understandably don't like that it's not F2P like other live service games. However, this way you're not getting pushed microtransactions via predatory tactics (e.g. P2W, loot box gambling and battle pass FOMO). It's worth considering on a sale if you find the price too steep.[*][b]First impressions[/b]: This game was written off by people ever since its reveal, it looked derivative, like a Guardians-themed Overwatch clone. It's a superficial judgement that I initially shared as well. I ended up trying the game and enjoyed it, but I'd imagine the internet echo chamber is making it difficult for others to do the same.[*][b]Characters[/b]: A common complaint is that the character designs are uninspiring and boring. I understand they're supposed to be a ragtag team of everyday people from the Concord universe, but I agree. They could've expanded on this with the character skins, but it's just comprised of basic palette swaps. This directly inhibits sense of progression as well, because they're rewarding you with these underwhelming skins.[*][b]Pronouns[/b]: The character selection screen includes pronouns for each character. A lot of people are [i]genuinely [/i]aggravated by this. It's not even prominently displayed - I didn't even notice the text until I saw all the comments about it.[*][b]Performance[/b]: It's pretty badly optimised. To get a stable framerate, I'm playing on DLSS Ultra Performance preset with everything set to low. It's crashed a couple times without any error messages, but is fortunately quite rare. There have been some performance patches already, but I expect it will take a while to fully iron things out.[*][b]Community feedback[/b]: The devs listen to players; they addressed a lot of major issues reported in the beta by launch, which were about a month apart.[*][b]Match length[/b]: The matches are short and don't drag on, I'd say no more than 10 minutes.[*][b]Gameplay[/b]: Gunplay is solid. Abilities are simple to grasp and roles don't feel restrictive - healers can hold their own. I still don't have a main because I find each hero is fun enough to swap between, depending on the situation. There are no ultimates, probably to maintain pacing and avoid major game swings with a click of a button.[*][b]Strategy[/b]:[b] [/b]There's some strategy sprinkled in with the idea of variants, which encourages building your own roster with different passives, and switching between roles in-game to stack the relevant crew bonuses you'd need.[*][b]Audio[/b]: Very well done - SFX is satisfying and I can easily pinpoint where enemies are spatially (which is great if I could actually hit them afterwards)[*][b]Release date[/b]: This shared a release date with Black Myth, one of the most anticipated games of the year. This may have contributed to the lower numbers, but I'm not sure how much of a difference it would've actually made.[*][b]PSN account[/b]: It requires a PSN account, which isn't available everywhere. Some people don't trust Sony with their data or hate having to make another account. We're also coming right off the back of the Helldivers 2 controversy around this topic, which may have left a sour taste in people's mouths.[*][b]Crossplay[/b]: It's enabled by default and[b] should stay on[/b] for fast matchmaking. There aren't many PC players (there are dozens of us... dozens!)[/list][b]Conclusion[/b]The core gameplay is solid. The pricing method is a healthy thing for consumers. The devs are trying new things with a new IP - they seem like they have good intentions and listen to community feedback. There are performance issues on launch, but it looks it's currently being addressed.There's a strange herd mentality praying for Concord's downfall, which feels unjustified because the studio hasn't really done anything [i]wrong[/i]. I hope it manages to survive, because I think this will ultimately hurt the kind of games we'll see in the future if it doesn't.

[h2] Concord: What it is & what it isn't [/h2][i] This review was written after 25+ hours of playtime during the closed and open beta, as well as time spent on the PlayStation 5 version. [/i][h3] What it is: [/h3]Concord is a unique spin on the Hero Shooter genre. What's good here are the fundamentals of a hero shooter: characters, modes, and balancing. I think Firewalk Studios nailed these crucial aspects and it leads to a game that just feels fun to play. Characters are all incredibly diverse and all play vastly different from one another. Exploring each Freegunner is a highlight to find which playstyle works best for you. Enemies can be countered easily and from what I can tell, there isn't a particular Freegunner at the moment that is too OP and is seen being played by at least someone in every match.The foundation is here, and it is solid. Actually playing the game extremely fun. The current set of game modes, casual and competitive, are a blast to play. Maps are detailed, performance on my rig is excellent, shooting mechanics feel great, and a lot of the weird grips the game had during the beta are ironed out.[h3] What it isn't: [/h3]Concord isn't great at showing off its more unique mechanics and how they work. There is a mechanic in the game under the Freegunners tab called Crew Builder that encourages you to essentially build a roster of characters. Building a roster can gain you specific buffs that will be activated when you play ...at least, that is how I think it works? I have no idea. It isn't explained at all in any capacity that I have seen. There's no tutorial or popup card explaining how it works and so I've just never used it.Furthermore, there is a Galactic Guide that, when clicked on, opens up a huge map and is sprinkled with lore and tidbits about the game and its universe. But ...that's it? I don't know what it's for or why I should care about it. I open it to get the free 100 XP to my "Lore Level" and what's a Lore Level? Again, no idea.Concord also isn't free. This is a paid hero shooter in 2024 where free to play live service games reign supreme. That's something that would stop someone even a little curious (though with the player count we saw during the open beta, I am not sure many are even keen on giving it a try). Even though the cost of entry is smaller than most new games released, I don't see all but the most curious of people forking over some dough to try it.[h3] What's the verdict? [/h3]You can tell that time, effort, and love was poured into the most important parts of what makes a Hero Shooter great. But the things that should make this game stand out fall flat with either bad execution, poor explanation, or no explanation at all. I want this game to succeed. I want more people to play it and experience how fun it is. I hope with time, the things that Concord isn't are ironed out, the game improves, and it finds the audience this game so desperately needs to survive.

I think if this game had released in this state as a free to play beta, people would be willing to give it a lot more leeway. As it stands, I think this game has interesting individual parts, but no cohesion between those pieces. The biggest compliments I can give this game is that the graphics are beautiful, the lore seems well thought out, and the fundamental gunplay and handling feels suberb. I think the performance, gameplay, systems surrounding that gameplay, and overall monetization model should not have released in this state. I've almost never had frame drops this bad on a 4090 and I typically run Cyberpunk 60fps ultra settings. Trying to run this game at 60 fps with DLSS quality mode on STILL gives me frequent frame drops and even two crashes so far.Overwatch 1 was able to release as a full-priced game 10 years ago because it was a trailblazer going down an unmarked path. With how saturated the market is becoming with games of this type, it's insane to me that they decided to not make this a freemium game. Realistically, what is this game providing to you for $40/$60 that Overwatch or Marvel Rivals won't be able to provide to you for free?One of my biggest pet peeves after having played for 6 hours are how short the games are. Granted, its been a while since I played Overwatch, but from what I remember the games in Overwatch usually last about twice as long as those in this game. The crew system places an emphasis on switching between characters in order to unlock the crew upgrade associated with that character's trait, but games barely last long enough to actually be able to utilize them. Having played a significant amount of time as the sniper character, Vale, you usually want to choose a character with faster reload and another with increased mobility in order to make the experience as a sniper more fluid. By that point, half the game has already ended. It seems really weird to me that to get Vale up to par with other characters you need to spend half the game playing as other charactersIf you want to know how this game revolutionizes the genre or how it tries to move the medium forward, the answer is that it doesn't. I think this game needed a couple more months in the oven to be able to set itself apart from the others in its genre. I want nothing more than for a game in this genre to dethrone Overwatch considering how far its fallen, but this game isn't it. The skeleton is there, the meat is just spoiled.*Side note*: Why the heck is this game tagged as a Political Sim?

Well I'd been playing this game nightly ever since it released, trying to earn the achievements and improve my skills with all the characters, only to come home and find out that Sony has given up on Concord three weeks in, as if it's failure wasn't largely their fault. This isn't the first time a niche FPS I like has bit the dust, see Hyperscape and the entire Titanfall franchise, but this one hurts a little more because this was the first Hero Shooter I ever really liked playing.The failure of Concord comes down to a lot of intersecting factors but it is nevertheless shocking to see a game this feature complete with this much effort and lore put into it that is just gone, after less than 3 weeks. The announcement says they are exploring other options, like maybe a F2P relaunch, and I dearly hope that's true, but I'm not holding my breath. If more people had been willing to overlook the superficial deficiencies of this game I feel like a very interesting PVP sandbox would have emerged. Rivalry is one of the most interesting and well thought out gamemodes I have ever played in this type of shooter.At the end of the day, Concord's failure to attract an audience can likely be attributed to the fact that in modern gaming, games are not given a chance to breathe, and must succeed immediately, combined with poor marketing and the fact that the FPS genre is one of the most impenetrable markets in gaming. Just about every permutation has a central pillar that any other challengers will always be in the shadow of. Cod,Overwatch,Fortnite,Apex, they have all locked down their parcels of land and it's been basically impossible for anything else to break out. The only thing that really sets Concord apart from the rest of the FPS graveyard at this point is the gap between the quality of this game and the magnitude of it's failure, which is surpassed maybe only by Titanfall 2, arguably the best example of a 10/10 FPS flop.Someday I hope Concord returns and I can play it again, and that it finds an audience when it does. Until then, all I'll have are the experiences I had playing it. If and when it does come back, if you bothered to read this review for whatever reason, I hope you give it a shot. It might surprise you.

*Disclaimer* From the top add 70 hours of play time in the Beta weekends to my time played, if you hold any value in that stat when reading reviews.**If the game is dead, why are my queues popping faster than OW queues?**I have been hovering over writing this review for a little while, mostly on the basis that I rant a lot and I'm not 100% certain on what angle to approach this from. I can find it difficult to keep my views concise, I will however try my best. *Disclaimer over*[h1]Remember when games were made with a 'player fun first' attitude?[/h1][h2]Why a price tag is important[/h2]In design philosophy Concord reminds me fondly of an older generation of shooting games like Battlefield up to BF1 or even something like OW1. You play the game and you are rewarded for doing so, you want skins for the character you like? play them. You want something fancy for your player card? play the game. You want to unlock that new character variant? Complete the challenges. Remember when I didn't have to be nickel and dimed for every little thing in a video game? Yes the aforementioned games had loot boxes, albeit with a fair delivery system, those are not present here you can see everything you are working toward all the way through.See with a $40 tag up front the devs have been freed to make a game that is based on being a fun game to play rather than being a repetitive husk designed to push players into a shop or underwhelming battlepass over and over again in order to feed to greedy beast up top. If you are the type to buy literally anything in a f2p then within 6 months of playing Concord you will have already spent less on it than in most f2p games.After a few hours of playing I was honestly struck by a refreshing reminder; 'I'm having fun!' like in the way I used to have fun. I am not feeling like I have to sweat like crazy and play characters I don't want to in a meta that has been diluted to the skill floor to be as appealing to as wide of an audience as possible. No I am having actual 'fun.'[h2]The Gameplay[/h2]Do you like Destiny? or Halo? this is essentially the gameplay style, with kits and a deck builder style system built in, more on this later)Like with Destiny, movement is fluid, I use the term fluid over fast purposefully. While some characters are definitely built more for speed than others, this is not a tweaky shooter. Every action is meant to be taken with purpose, every button press is impactful. Expect double jumps, glides, and dodges and a tonne of flair available at the player's fingertips.Character kits feel honestly perfect, While there are roles in the game, and they are important, the characters all function essentially as damage dealers in essence. The devs have clearly taken inspiration from other games in the market and have really iterated upon them, once or twice I and others I have played with have openly said 'oh, this character is kinda like X other character from X other game, if that character was designed with fun in mind.' The abilities are well distributed and make sense in each given kit, and while there are characters that are more easy to access the skill floor of than others the game never goes to the point of disregarding the importance of skill expression and the ceiling. What I am saying here is that you will never feel like you have been cheesed when you die.The TTK is a bit longer too, remember I said how every button press is impactful? This is why. If you want to secure a kill you are going to have to work for it, expect to have to use all of your kit in a good rotation to be able to secure kills. there is real tactical depth to every fight and everything counts.. you find yourself out of cooldowns? you better consider retreating unless you have some serious aim skills to prevail. No big 'I win' buttons either. No ultimates is a fantastic decision here and perfectly matches the games tactful intentions.Sound design is phenomenal, the weapons punch and kick. and the abilities all have wonderful audio and visual feedback and keep the player immersed and informed. The same follows for the games aesthetic design with every character model looking highly distinct from one another and instantly recognisable once you have gotten to know them. I don't want to delve to hard into graphics in this review, but I will say this, the attention to detail on the assets is insane.[h2]The Crew Builder[/h2]As briefly as possible - In this game you are rewarded for playing multiple roles. Each role has a corresponding buff (faster reload, quicker dodge cd, better range fall off etc.) There are 6 in totalYou want to play just one character all game? sure, you can do that. if you are really good you will stomp, but. Whenever you die and swap role, you will bring the buff from the last role you played with you, collect as many as you like (up to 6) and essentially 'build' the character you want to get to.The Crew Builder essentially works like a deck builder, with each character and each variant of a character being a card. Choose your roster of 12 cards. I am not very good at explaining this system, but I'm sure others have done it very well, so I refer you to them.. it's very good and very in depth.[h2] Final thoughts [/h2]I have fallen in love with this game, and I think honestly 90% of people who play this game will feel the same way.The media coverage of this game has been disingenuous at best, infactual at times, and outright abhorrent at worst. and some of the discourse around the game is quite obviously in VERY bad faith. On a personal level I find it deeply upsetting that we have allowed hateful political discourse to enter into the gaming space that is supposed to be about escaping the real world with characters that we relate to / dream of being. Shame on those people.**May I just assure you that, yes, this game has pronouns in the character select. will it affect your experience? no. It's completely unobtrusive and will impact your game in any way, you can ignore it, but someone out there will feel happy to be represented by it.. it's as simple as that.**I would strongly recommend anyone to play the game and form their own opinion from gameplay before switching off of this one. Does it have flaws? sure it has some rough edges and sometimes it really does not put it's best foot forward but the devs have been very receptive to feedback.If you are interested, maybe have questions, or just want to see some gameplay then I am streaming this nearly every day. Please feel free to hop in and see for yourself and ask any question you like. https://www.twitch.tv/mnkyjamjamI am super excited for a bright future for this game.Sorry for rambling and thanks for reading!

After spending about 7 hours with Concord, my feelings are mixed. The emphasis on a $40 live-service model feels risky, making it a tough sell for most players. The game is short on modes, and the ones available lack inspiration. Matches often feel decided within the first minute, with few options to turn the tide. While not every hero shooter needs an Ultimate ability, Concord desperately needs a system or mechanic to make matches more engaging.The game's approach to lore, with its supposed weekly cutscenes, is puzzling. The opening cinematic fails to make you care about or invest in any of the charactersthey just exist in a world that feels like a low-budget knockoff of the MCU, complete with poor characterization and mediocre writing that attempts to mimic the MCU's humor, which never really worked to begin with. Maybe it's my ADHD talking, but reading page after page of text in the Constellation section is one of the most boring and pointless lore systems I've encountered in a game. Lore is essentialor a game developer to create a framework for a character or world, but simply dumping it into the game and expecting players to understand or care about it is baffling.Where Concord shines is in its first-person shooter gameplay. Its fast, chaotic, and challenging. Despite some truly awful character designs, most of the characters play well and have distinct playstyles. For example, Teo appeals to those who enjoy Call of Duty-style FPS gameplay, while Kyps is all about stealth. There's a good variety in character gameplay, so most players will likely find someone they enjoy playing as.However, the level design is lackluster. If someone asked me to name my favorite level, I wouldnt be able to do much more than vaguely descr"the one with the crates and the glowing thing in the middle." Hero shooters succeed when you become invested not just in the characters but in the levels as well. Remember how exciting it was in Overwatch to play on a mini Las Vegas level or a deserted cowboy western level? Concord has none of that. Its levels are bland and uninspired, all feeling fundamentally the same, even if the color palettes differ. Like the characters, the levels seem to just exist without any continuity in art style or memorable locations. They all blend together, making it difficult to learn or distinguish one level from another.Matchmaking is also concerning. While Steam data should be taken with a grain of salt, as of this writing, Concord hasnt even reached a peak of 1,000 players. Currently, only 248 people are playing on Steam. If youre on PC and want to play against other PC players only, youll face match wait times of 5-10 minutes. You have to enable crossplay to fill player slots with PS5 players, but the low player count leads to matches where everyone has poor connections.the recent players Ive fought, most were from the US, and since Im based in Europe, it results in a poor performance experience.On PC, the games performance is erratic. My 5900X with a 6800 XT GPU should be more than enough to run the game smoothly, but regardless of the settings, the game runs poorly, fluctuating between 150 FPS and 45 FPS within seconds.The game is literally causing me motion sickness. I contacted Firewalk support, and they suggested that the issue might be related to region or server problems. Being in Europe, Im consistently matched with players from the US, which could be contributing to the games sluggish performance.Concord isnt a bad game, but its pricing is way off for the market its competing in. The game modes lack excitement, the characters struggle to be likable, and the level design is bland. However, its a solid first-person multiplayer shooter with intense and occasionally excellent combat.Given the low player interest, I can only recommend Conc are okay with spending $40 and willing to take the risks mentioned here. I will continue to play Concord for at least a week or two, just to see where the game lands both with players but also to see how the completely nonsensical story might evolve.

It's unfortunately very difficult to talk about Concord right now without addressing the bizarre reactionary current swimming around it; long story short the game has pronouns in its character bios and the main cast are a diverse group and, while I can understand the designs not gelling with some people the "anti-woke" crowd have decided to make this their new target of their pointless culture war so I'm just going to start off by saying that I think Concord is a good, fun game that, while it has some flaws and is competing against free games in a very competitive market does have some legitimate potential to grow into something really cool and special if it finds an audience to sustain it. And that I think all of the right-wing grifters swimming around this game begging it to fail because they see any diversity in anything as some sort of "attack on white people" or whatever can go bugger off and hopefully learn to grow up sooner rather than later.Okay, that out the way (and apologies to those actually just here for a real review of the game), how is it?Well it's a snappy, fun, multiplayer arena hero shooter. It's definitely got a bit of a learning curve to it, I think the higher time to kill and emphasis on using dodges takes some adjustment but it's one I've come to like. Gunfights can become quite sustained and crazy affairs and, while I don't want to leave anyone out by comparing it to something else that many of you may not have played, it's be very difficult for me to not mention Destiny PvP as the feeling of the gunplay really reminds me of it in a lot of ways so, if you like how Destiny 2's guns feel I feel like you'll have a fair idea of what to expect (although I gotta say some of the sounds on thee guns are wonderfully punchy, just adds a lot to the feel of them).Now Hero shooters typically go for payload-style objectives/more linear straight line maps that funnel teams together but Concord is more into its circular arenas which is a double-edged sword, on one hand it doesn't feel like you always get those constant insane team vs team clashes in the same way a lot of hero shooters like to do but on the other hand the maps to leave a lot of room for flanks and fights that aren't just stuck in one section of the map the whole time but I will say that, if you're looking for that overwatch feeling, this game is providing something else and you won't get those team fights in quite the same way.In terms of characters the playstyles on offer here are pretty diverse but the focus is always still on that more lethal gunplay aspect; you're not going to have healers healing more damage than you can dish out here, they're not some essential component even though they are helpful and the game definitely doesn't have the same emphasis on team comp in its less competitive modes (even though understanding team com obviously can give you an advantage). Good gunplay and skill usage wins the day here more than a character dominating solely because of who they are and not the person playing them. That said it does help add to the fact that, even in casual modes, this game wants you switching characters by giving you perks for a match based on the characters you previously played. Don't listen to the people complaining about the game being "woke" or being so-called "generic slop." The truth is, Concord is an incredibly fun hero-shooter. There are so many things to like about this game.The cinematic vignettes (cutscenes that tell a story with the playable characters and the galaxy) are a real treat to watch, and a new one is getting released every week, with plans for more each Season. The game doesn't have MTX at launch, although there will be an item shop starting in Season 1 in October.THERE WILL NOT BE A BATTLE PASS IN CONCORD!All of the playable characters ("Freegunners") are incredibly different from each other and extremely fun to play. Unlike other hero shooters, the roles (classes) that the Freegunners fall into in Concord are very different compared to games like Overwatch. Every character is designed to be capable of decent DPS output, with the role descriptions detailing what each one is designed to do outside of that. What's also unlike Overwatch is that the playable characters don't have ultimates, which I personally love, because it means you have to rely more heavily on the characters' base kits and abilities (of which they have 2), rather than waiting for a cooldown to release a cheap move that turns the tables of the game. Concord also does not place a heavy emphasis on having medic characters: there are heal pads scattered around all the maps, which grant regen healing when picked up before going on a cooldown, and there are only two Freegunners at launch with team healing capabilities; both of their heals are regen-heals as well.There are very interesting mechanics in Concord that you either don't really see anywhere else, or don't see anywhere else period. The one I like the most is the crew bonus system: a mechanic that lightly discourages picking a main and sticking with them by granting role-specific boosts upon respawn/next round every time you change classes that stack to give you a slight edge. These bonuses include faster movement speed, better recoil control, faster dodge cooldown, and more. This system is actually very casual-player friendly, because since they're granted upon respawn (aka dying), if you decide to accumulate unique crew bonuses every time you die, you could potentially turn the tide of a match by powering up your character.The maps, planets, aesthetic and general presentation of Concord, both in the visuals and the sound, is genuinely beautiful. From Daniel Pemberton's (Spiderverse movie series) atmospheric and uptempo synth-filled music, to the Freegunners' character designs and colour palettes, to the sheer amount of colours you see in each map, Concord really is a sight for sore eyes.While the game does have some performance issues on PC that need to be addressed sooner rather than later, I simply cannot recommend Concord as a game enough: I think it's more than worth the price of admission (and I paid extra to play it early!) Please consider trying the game for an hour or so before deciding that it's simply not a good game, because in my personal opinion, it has the potential to be my favourite hero-shooter ever made.

[Disclaimer: I played 30 hours of this game between the closed and open Beta]Concord is a perfect team shooter. period.Concord is a beautifully crafted game with an amazing amount of thought and insight woven into every aspect of the game. The gameplay is simple enough to pick up but has a surprising about of depth in its mechanics to discover and master. Instead of your typical tank/healer/dps rolls, concord opts for a much more flexible and less defined rolls that allow its 5 player teams to consist of any combination of freegunners without punishment. Each freegunner has only 2 abilities but all have completely different movement and passives. Theyre easy to pick up and fun to master.The Crew bonus system is GENIUSthe game encourages swapping characters by granting you additional passives (eg reload speed, movement speed) when you swap to different classes during respawns. You can only gain this buff by dying to an enemy player. this crafts a system of gameplay/stratagey around an element of competitive gameplay (dying/respawning) that has been mostly untouched by other games. At no point during a match are you not participating in the game competitively, even when you're losing. This also works as a great balancing mechanic, if you and your teamates arn't losing, you don't gain buffs you don't need. while the enemy team can use these buffs as a catch up mechanic if they can utilize them successfully. this leads to a lot of matches being less one sided and more exciting.Character designs are stunning.Concord art direction is unmatched, each character feels interesting and unique while the game itself has a strong visual identity that ties it all together beautifully.If you enjoy lore and world building there is also an absolutely HUGE amount of unlockable story in the Galatic guide menu, including character bios and a 100 years of in game history to discover. As you level up you'll unlock more lore and cosmetics and as you level up each of your freegunners, you will unlock even more cosmetics exclusive to them.NO MICRO TRANSACTIONS!!!I cannot believe how refeshing it is to buy a hero shooter and not have to worry about fomo, battle passes, loot boxes or micro transactions. Firewalk studio is committed to making a game you buy ONCE and have access to ALL its content for free. Including new Freegunners, cosmetics and in game events and modes.The elephant in the room.Concord is very diverse with its characters. Not only does every character bio have pronouns, but there is a diverse range of species, gender, sexuality and race. Bazz is trans, Daveers is nonbinary, It-z has two moms, there are a lot of POC characters and even Lennox is basically a white guy (green alien). What im trying to say is this game does DEI right. It isnt a gimmick, it isnt done for publicity, it is just unashamedly and honestly very progressive. As a queer person this feels like the first time ive ever experienced that in a game.HOWEVER, this obviously annoys a lot of bigots and this has lead to a hate campaign to smear the games reputation in hopes it fails. I bring this up because you will see a lot of bad faith criticism about an objectively great game based entirely in "anti-woke", alt right idiology. Don't let it fool you, this game is amazing and if you give it a chance you'll be welcomed into one of the nicest communities ive ever been a part of.score: 10/10. DONT MISS OUT!!

Now that I played it for a lot longer, I wanted to fill this out.I've played a lot of Overwatch, Destiny, Halo, and some CoD.I have felt disappointed by them all for some big and small reasons, but ultimately stopped playing FPS games because I ended up feeling taxed by the game and the way the companies that made them were asking for money.Now that I've played this game, I'll say, the shooting and movement feel amazing. Almost this entire time I've enjoyed being able to try out different characters, and they way they make the buff system encourages people to switch, so I almost always get to pick something that fits the moment and my buff sequence. I've found that to be the most subjective disagreement, but it is clear the art team put everything they had into everything in this game. The programmers too.The thing it took me the longest to appreciate is how the matches feel from beginning to end, and here I think this game shines. They feel pretty quick, but I think when there are two teams that are evenly matched, it can go longer and really feel like a push and pull. I feel like it is pretty fast paced, and especially the objective based feels good.Overall, I like the game the more I play it, it's becoming positively exciting to play games.
