Upon first seeing Concord announced at a trade show several months ago, I'll admit that I was disappointed that it was going to be another hero shooter. I personally thought the characters looked interesting, I appreciated the color and vibrancy of the world and enjoyed the lighthearted dialogue. Once gameplay was shown, however, I wasn't super enthused. I am not the biggest fan of multiplayer shooters these days, mostly due to toxic communities compounded by players who follow the classic toxic Twitch streamers (yes I'm old).I try to keep an open mind when it comes to games, so even with all of that in mind, I jumped into the PS5 beta and gave the game a shot. What I found was what I consider an impressive roster of 16 characters (plus Variants, but personally I don't think they offer enough variety to be considered a separate character from their counterparts), engaging gameplay, nice visuals, and progression unlocks for skins and other cosmetics.After four or five hours played in the beta, I found myself interested in purchasing Concord. Is it a hero shooter? Yes. Is it generic? In some ways, yes. But there's enough here to differentiate it and make it entertaining from my perspective.What's are some things that are different from other hero shooters I've played?Shorter matches. I've seen people compare it to Destiny PVP, and while the mechanics are different I can see where that comparison comes from. Characters have a variety of movement options, some of which feel very close to classes in Destiny, and again the short matches make it easy to fit in quite a few even during a short session. Most matches that I've played in last under 10 minutes. I understand this can be a pro or a con depending on how you look at it. I've found myself wishing some of the objective modes went to a bit of a higher score but we'll see what they release in the future.Lore. Concord seems to have put a fair amount of time into not only developing the characters but the world itself. There's a map of the galaxy containing dozens and dozens of entries, some which unlock as you progress, that give you a few paragraphs here and there of information that helps build an understanding of the world they're trying to create. I don't think Lore is unique to Concord, but they way they deliver it is kind of cool and I find it interesting.Abilities: I won't say I've played every hero shooter, but there are times where it feels like the shooting is second-tier to the abilities. In Concord, I've found myself getting most of my kills with my primary weapon while the abilities act as a way to support the damage I'm able to do with my weapon(s). I haven't yet played every character, but most of them that I have played have had abilities that are enjoyable and easy to understand.Crews: You build your own roster based on which characters you'd like to play in your matches. I haven't played the more competitive modes, but from what I understand once a character is killed, you have to swap to a different character in those modes, so that makes Crews more impactful in those modes. In the casual deathmatch/objective modes, it allows me to select which crew bonuses I want to have and make sure my favorite characters are front and center.Crew Bonuses: When you select your character, you will see the Crew Bonus they provide. This can be something like increased mobility, increased reload speed, or faster dodge recharge, for example. After you die with that character that bonus is unlocked for other characters you play during that match (I honestly am not sure if it counts if you keep playing the same character, so someone feel free to chime in if they do know). This is a cool way to encourage players to swap characters during matches and change their tactics based on situations. It's also a nice way to say 'hey I don't like how slow this character reloads, but otherwise they're awesome' and realize that you can start matches with another character who gives improved reload speed and then swap to who you want to play. It adds a really light layer of strategy to the game that although simple, is satisfying.I've gone on long enough but I do want to say that it's a shame that the state of gaming today is a default hate towards anything new; calling it immediately 'generic', a 'cash grab', 'trash', 'boring', you get it. I, for one, am always excited to see companies developing new IP and, even if the characters are in some cases derivative of other characters in movies, games, or tv shows, and even if the gameplay isn't this monumental redefinition of the genre, it's still something new. As someone who has grown tired of a lot of the same multiplayer shooters releasing on a yearly cadence with little to no change, it's nice to see something that feels new to me. Whether or not you agree is fine, but I would say that overall I recommend this game to anyone who is interested in the way it looks, the way it plays, or just supporting something that manages to feel a bit new to some of us.I hope that this review helps inform those of you that are on the fence so that you can make a decision that you're happy with. Hope to see some of you in game.

*Also played 15 hours of the beta + 1 hour of pre-launch on PS5*TLDR: It's a good game with undeserved hate (But yes the character designs are not that appealing) if you can get over the character designs you can have a great time.Concord is a 5 vs 5 hero shooter with the spirit of Destiny/Halo gunplay.The gameplay is very tight and satisfying. The sound design is a major factor in this, hit marker sounds have a satisfying ping and each gun has weight. The foundation is there and is more polished than the majority of games. A common critique for Concord is the lack of innovation or new ideas. But Concord has 3 distinct mechanics.Crew System Perks -Each character has a perk i.e. reload speed bonus, decreased cooldown on dodge. When you die, the perk of the previous character gets passed on to the next hero you choose. This encourages you to pick hero's you don't usually play before picking your main. I like this system because the benefits are rewarding. Vale, for example has 1 shot in her gun. So if you pick a character with faster reload before Vale it will help you a ton.Dodge -In Concord the ability to dodge to get out of gunfights is a great feature. This feature isnt a hail mary, you will still get punished for reckless decisions. Furthermore each character has benefit with the dodge i.e. going invisible or a speed boost.Persistent Gadgets-And the final feature is persistent gadgets on the battlefield, meaning your health pads or mines will stay in the game unless it is destroyed even if you switch characters. Which is good for making set ups and helping your team before going one army mode with Star Child.Concord has 16 distinct characters at launch (with new ones being free too) and 6 game modes but at the moment I haven't tried their search and destroy mode. This is a unique spin of search because if you win a round with a character, that character is locked for you. Therefore your friends may have to be the ones who carry sometimes :)The PC performance needs to be addressed and ere are some bugs and kinks. The most important of a shooter is the gunplay and this game delivers. I can easily see myself putting more hours.8/10 in my book.

For once, I feel like i need to warn anyone who reads this message before purchasing the game.Starting with the simple aesthetics, the characters really look like they came out of a B-grade sci-fi movie shot in the '80s. Despite the alien origins of some of the characters, they just look like underpaid actors with a lot of makeup on, hoping to make them appear as if they come from other worlds, when in reality, their overly humanoid shape suggest otherwise.The narrative universe is very well crafted in terms of lore and i really enjoyed exploring the interactive galaxy map reading all the littles notes and bits about the planets and the worlds' stories, but all of this unfortunately plays a very marginal role since the game is anything but story-driven.As for the actual gameplay, only a tiny portion of the characters are enjoyable to play. Setting aside personal preferences, I don't believe anyone would ever have fun with some of the characters in the roster due to their slow movement, extremely tedious gimmicks, or simple inability to excel in areas where other champions clearly outperform them.The shooting mechanics are smooth, but many of the weapons are very frustrating to use, and it's very likely that you'll find a champion whose abilities you love but whose weapons you hate, or vice versa.Additionally, some champions are completely on another level compared to others, capable of dealing significant damage to enemies in a short time while also being nearly untouchable due to their durable nature or extreme mobility, further narrowing down the pool of champions that actually make sense to choose.The maps are a bit too big, sometimes resulting in long periods of wandering while searching for action after respawning. There are few strategic points to defend and many open areas (or areas with many connected paths), making flanking extremely easy even for characters who are supposed to play other roles.The overall movement speed also seems to be rather low for the genre, at times giving the impression of moving on the moon or, when trying to run, in a nightmare.Bugs are there but, fortunately, i never encountered major ones (it's common for your character's hands to go completely invisible from time to time)The price also seems rather high, limiting the player base that could sustain the game once the initial hype (if any) wears off, putting it at a disadvantage compared to other free-to-play titles.Honestly, I don't think Concord can become the new hit of the genre or dethrone already existing and more established titles, but it might offer a few dozen hours of fun before becoming repetitive or frustrating once you understand the game's meta.

(I purchased the Deluxe Edition to play this game in advanced access)TL;DR - The game is good. A lot of people made judgement calls on the games quality based on a couple of character designs they didn't like, but putting those criticisms aside it's quite the solid multiplayer shooter experience.In terms of what to expect - You might look at the cast and the trailers and assume paralells between it and other "hero shooters" and it does have some aspects of those, but if you want something to compare it against gameplay wise it feels remarkably like Destiny.It's a dedicated Destiny PvP game, with no battle pass, just a one time $40 USD payment.good objective based modes, casual and permadeath modes, and mechanics that carry through all of them (switching characters is important, for instance) - The presence of TDM modes with less of an objective focus can make some of the map design a little awkward (it's clear they were weighted to flow around KOTH/Capture points) and many TDM games boil down to a death funnel in one central room, but that is literally true of any First Person Shooter.all the characters feel distinct and different from each other, and it all feels very well balanced. No one hero feels significantly stronger than the other. They're all very well voice acted, their silhouettes are all distinct and instantly identifiable in a gunfight. Good variety to the skins available at launch, granted a good majority of them are recolours, but the legendary options available at launch give me high hopes for the detail and creativity we'll see with the future legendary offerings. Lots to tweak and unlock for your favorite hero as well with their individual accessory slot, be it goggles, rings, etc, as well as individual weapon and character charms!THE LORE IS INCREDIBLE. Honestly loving the game so far.What I like:- Performance and visuals are both stellar. No hitches so far.- Despite the doom and gloomers, matchmaking has been extremely fast. Usually 30-40 seconds, but sometimes far less. Seems consistent across the two playlists I've tried so far.- Art direction and aesthetic is great.- Audio is really satisfying, and voicelines are well produced- Weekly lore cutscenes are a cool spin, looking forward to seeing where that goes.- Only one disconnect issue, and it was Steam going down.- Lots of combat variety between the different "freegunners", with unlockable variants.- THe "crew building" bonuses that power you up for playing multiple heroes in a single match are also really unique. Like rolling a tank gives you increased healing for the rest of the match. Or playing a healer gives increased reload speed the rest of the match. I typically play one hero per match in a lot of hero games, which means if someone else picks it I'm bummed the whole time. In this I'm playing 4-5 per match and getting rewarded for it. Stuff like starting as a healer and deploying heals, then swapping on death...the heal pads remain. This is REALLY cool for strategy over the length of a match.- It takes teamwork to win, whether kills or objectives. Which means there are a lot of steamrolls for teams that don't regroup and stuff. HOWEVER, you get 4500xp per match, and only 500 for winning. So with all of the jobs/objectives/challenges (there's so many) every match feels like a ton of progress. Heroes leveling, profile leveling, variants unlocking, cosmetics unlocking, all constantly.- Good balance changes since beta, including the ability for people to join matches in progress AND punishment for leaving early.- Damage feels wayyyy more punchy. PS5 had the benefit of haptics helping, but PC now feels like you're doing damage. Hit detection also seems far more solid, whether due to improvements in the game or servers I'm not sure.- While it's season 0, I'm currently excited that all content will be free.Primary feedback I'd like to see addressed:- Respawns closer to teammates would be great. Some of the longer/linear maps its near impossible to regroup.- Party chat defaults "off" meaning its impossible to coordinate. I get people not wanting to talk but let them opt out, vs making them opt in.- Ping is "moving here" and "warning here". Would love a wheel like "healing here", "regroup here", "hold here", etc.- Weekly cutscenes don't need to play every time I launch the game. Yes they can be skipped but just play it once and let me play it again.- Players seem to have no clue about the bonuses for swapping, or how powerful they can be. Encouraging this would be nice.- Players suck at playing objectives like in most shooters, incentivizing objectives with higher XP rewards would be great.All-in-all, a game I'll keep dipping back into. It's by no means a carbon copy of anything, and instead a polished shooter that borrows some things and innovates others. Scratches the arena shooter itch without needing to playing linear objective modes in Overwatch, or watching people slide and dive all over in COD.

These characters feel very, very good to play.The most fundamental thing a game needs to be is fun. So many new games are simply not very fun, for all their production value. And this game is freaking FUN! My fiancee and I had a blast just aimlessly messing around in the practice area, let alone actually playing matches. Movement, weapons, and abilities all feel satisfying.Sound design is sublime. First of all, firing off your weapons and abilities is just euphonic, very satisfying to the ears. Chef's kiss. But the sound design improves gameplay, too. You get so many rich audio cues, you can practically play with your eyes closed. For example, footsteps are very spatially accurate and even differ from character to character. When you play as Bazz, your footsteps are quieter, helping you sneak up for takedowns. When you charge around as Star Child, you can anticipate being heard and whip around proactively to catch anybody attracted by your booming steps. Pay attention to sound for a huge advantage.Balance is in a remarkably good state for just coming out. A couple classes might be a bit above or under the line, but overall, each character feels OP in their own way, and I don't feel like matches are unfair. You are heavily incentivized to swap characters throughout the match, as well. If you camp one character, you're missing out on Crew Bonuses that stack when you change classes.I am very optimistic for this game's future. Haters, please step aside and let us enjoy things.Wishlist:Ranked matchmaking modeCo-op PvE mode (like Team Fortress 2's Mann vs Machine, something chill for when you don't feel like competing)EDIT: I miss Concord </3 I'm playing Marvel Rivals now and wish I were playing Concord. It felt so good flying around as Haymar and Roka!
